docs.title: c4
docs.text:
c4 is a Python toolkit for genetics research on the UCSF C4 cluster. These pages cover its data loading layer: one catalog file that lists every dataset the lab uses, and a small API for finding, loading and merging them. They also cover its HLA tools, for working with HLA typing from HLA-HD and HIBAG, and fine-mapping of GWAS loci with SuSiE.

Example data

Every example on these pages uses a made-up cohort called demo, with fake patients, samples and paths. Real cohorts work the same way.

If you have access to the c4 repository (it is private to the lab), the demo is in examples/demo/ and you can follow along. From the repository root:

export C4_CATALOG=examples/demo/catalog.yaml
python examples/demo/run_examples.py    # runs every example on these pages

The docs show the demo's data folder as /data/lab; in the repository it is examples/demo/data.

docs.title: In 30 seconds
docs.text:
from c4.cohort import cohort

demo = cohort("demo")                          # prints what's available
pheno = demo.load("pheno")                     # one table, with patient_id added
df = demo.load("pheno", "pcs", "hla.hlahd")    # several tables, merged on patient_id
vcf = demo.path("dna.imputed", chrom=6)        # genetic data: a file path
demo.describe("OS_mo")                         # what does this column mean?
demo.check()                                   # is everything where the catalog says?

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
One catalog. Every data file is listed once in c4/catalog.yaml, grouped by cohort: phenotype tables, principal components, HLA calls by software, and DNA by data type. Paths live there, not in code, so when data moves only the catalog changes.

One patient ID. Different data types identify people differently: clinical tables use a patient ID, the exome VCF uses sequencing sample names, the array uses genotyping IDs. Each cohort has an ID map that links them all to a single patient_id. Every table you load gets a patient_id column, so merging anything with anything is a join on that one column.

Loud, not silent. Merges print how many patients matched. Duplicate patients stop a merge instead of quietly multiplying rows. Missing files and unlinked samples are reported rather than skipped.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
c4 needs Python 3.11+. In a clone of the repository, this installs it and every Python package it uses:

pip install -e .

Add ".[dev]" instead of . to also get pytest. Extracting variants and the survival/PRS commands also need bcftools on your PATH (on C4: module load bcftools). Fine-mapping needs plink2 and R with the susieR package (module load plink2 r).

Then check that the catalog matches what is on disk:

python -c "from c4.cohort import cohort; cohort('demo').check()"

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Installing c4 (pip install -e .) gives you the c4 command. c4 --help lists the commands, and c4 <command> --help shows every option. The full reference at the bottom of this page is generated from that same help text.

In the examples, replace COHORT with a cohort name from the data catalog.

Command What it does dosages Dosages for a few variants from a cohort's VCFs, with patient_id survival Cox PH survival test per variant prs Survival test of a weighted polygenic risk score clump LD-clump GWAS summary statistics against a VCF or PLINK panel finemap avail, finemap setup Build a per-session LD reference panel from a cohort's genetic data finemap loci Regions to fine-map, from one or more GWAS finemap run SuSiE-RSS on each locus, with LD from a finemap setup panel finemap visualize Plot fine-mapped loci: p-values, PIPs and genes concordance Genotype concordance between samples in two VCF/PLINK files vcf-overlap Variants shared by two VCFs genotype-correlation Per-sample Pearson r between two VCFs' dosages liftover Lift a file of variant positions to another genome build split-hla, merge-hla Switch HLA tables between A and A_1/A_2 columns hla_concordance Per-sample, per-gene concordance between two HLA call files convert-p Not yet implemented (planned: P-group conversion)

External tools needed on your PATH: bcftools for dosages, survival, prs, concordance, vcf-overlap and genotype-correlation; plink2 (or PLINK 1.9) for clump; plink2 for finemap setup; R with susieR for finemap run (on C4: module load r).

Writing variants

Variants are chr:pos:ref:alt, chr:pos:ref>alt or chr:pos; the chr prefix is optional. Quote anything with >: unquoted, the shell treats it as a redirect and writes to a file named after the ALT allele.

docs.title: Variants, survival and PRS
docs.text:
# Dosages for a few SNPs: one row per sample, plus snps.variants.tsv
c4 dosages --dataset COHORT --variants 6:32659999:A:G --variant-list more.txt -o snps.tsv

# One variant: prints a results table (add --km-plot km.png for a Kaplan-Meier plot)
c4 survival --dataset COHORT --variants '4:1455432:A>T' --survival OS

# Many variants in b37 (lifted to the VCFs' build automatically), saved to files
c4 survival --dataset COHORT --variant-list vars.txt --variant-build b37 --survival PFS \
    -o results.tsv --save-dosages dosages.tsv

# PRS: weights are a headerless 3-column TSV (variant_id, effect_allele, effect)
c4 prs --dataset COHORT --weights prs.tsv --survival OS --quantiles 5 -o prs_OS/
  • Dosage counts the ALT allele as you wrote it. If the VCF has the alleles the other way round, the dosage is flipped and the variant gets a warning. See Extracting variants for how matching works.
  • Covariates, endpoints and which VCFs to use come from the cohort's survival: block in the catalog.
  • --variant-build lifts variants with the catalog's chain files; give --chain-file to use another.
  • prs writes prs.log, individual_prs.tsv, prs_variants.tsv and plots into its output directory. The weights file must have exactly three columns; anything else is an error naming the line.
  • How the Cox models are set up (complete cases, PC standardisation, what the HR is per): c4.survival.

docs.title: Clumping
docs.text:
c4 clump results.PHENO.glm.logistic.hybrid panel.chr6.vcf.gz -o out/chr6 \
    --chr 6 --kgp-pops EUR --clump-p1 1e-5 --clump-r2 0.2 --clump-kb 500
  • GWAS and panel variants are matched on chromosome, position and alleles (REF/ALT swaps allowed), whatever ID scheme each uses.
  • For a per-chromosome panel, give one chromosome's file; the others are found by substituting into its chr<N>.
  • --kgp-pops subsets a 1000 Genomes panel to populations or super-populations.
  • Writes {out}.clumps, {out}.lead.tsv (index variants with their GWAS stats), {out}.dropped.tsv (unmatched variants, with a reason) and {out}.log.
  • plink2's --memory defaults to half of the SLURM or cgroup job limit, so it isn't killed on shared nodes. If the plink2 build has no --clump, PLINK 1.9 is used.

docs.title: Fine-mapping
docs.text:
c4 finemap avail                                               # genetic data you can build a panel from
c4 finemap setup --dna demo.imputed --panel-name demo --chr 6  # LD panel in $TMPDIR/demo/
c4 finemap loci results.PHENO.glm.linear --build b38 -o loci.tsv
c4 finemap run results.PHENO.glm.linear --loci loci.tsv --panel demo --build b38 --in-sample -o fm/pheno
c4 finemap visualize fm/pheno -o plots/                        # one plot per locus with a credible set

See Fine-mapping for how each step works, the output files, and how to check the results.

docs.title: Genotype QC
docs.text:
# Concordance between every sample pair across two files, plus within each file
c4 concordance array.vcf.gz exome.vcf.gz concordance.tsv --within

# Only specific pairs (file-1 ID, file-2 ID per line)
c4 concordance array.vcf.gz exome.vcf.gz concordance.tsv --between-pairs pairs.tsv

# Shared variants (CHROM POS), e.g. to subset both files first
c4 vcf-overlap array.vcf.gz imputed.vcf.gz overlap.tsv --remove-dup

# Per-sample correlation of dosages (DS) between two VCFs
c4 genotype-correlation vcf1.vcf.gz vcf2.vcf.gz corr.tsv --dosage --samples map.tsv

Concordance output: each between-file pair gets two rows. - all_exclHomRef: sites where the file-2 sample is homozygous reference are left out. - all_inclHomRef: all sites.

P2, P1 and P0 are the share of sites matching on 2, 1 or 0 alleles. Within-file pairs get one row, all. Variants are matched on chromosome, position and alleles; multi-allelic records are left out. On millions of variants it can be slow, so subset to shared positions first.

Correlation matches variants on CHROM, POS, REF and ALT. Without --dosage, genotypes are counted as non-reference alleles, so haploid calls work. --verbose writes the sums needed to combine results across chromosomes.

docs.title: Liftover of a variant file
docs.text:
c4 liftover hg19ToHg38.over.chain variants.bed variants_hg38.bed
c4 liftover hg19ToHg38.over.chain variants.txt variants_hg38.bed --chrom-col 0 --start-col 1
  • .bed input is 0-based, as BED is. For other files give --chrom-col and --start-col; positions are 1-based (as in VCFs) unless --zero-based.
  • Output is a 3-column BED file in input order. Rows that can't be lifted go to <output>.unmapped with the reason: not in the new build, mapping to several places, or a region that doesn't lift as one piece.
  • Uses pyliftover, like the variant liftover above. No R needed.

docs.title: HLA
docs.text:
c4 split-hla calls.csv calls_split.tsv --genes A,B --columns ID --digits 4
c4 merge-hla calls_split.tsv calls.tsv
c4 hla_concordance wes.csv imputed.csv --file1_id seqID --file2_id genotype_id -o hla_concordance.tsv

Name Type Description Default --install-completion boolean Install completion for the current shell. None --show-completion boolean Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation. None --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • convert-p: [Not yet implemented] Convert HLA alleles to P-group designations.
  • dosages: Extract dosages for a few variants from a cohort's VCFs.
  • finemap: Fine-mapping: LD reference panels built from the data catalog.
  • genotype-correlation: Compute per-sample Pearson r and r² between dosage vectors across two VCFs.
  • hla_concordance: Compare HLA typing between two files.

  • prs: Test a weighted polygenic risk score (PRS) for survival association.

  • vcf-overlap: Find overlapping variants between two VCF files.

docs.title: clump
docs.text:
LD-clump GWAS summary statistics using a VCF or PLINK genotype panel.

GWAS and panel variants are harmonized to CHROM:POS:REF:ALT before clumping (matching on the unordered allele pair, so REF/ALT swaps still match). Variants that can't be matched are reported with a reason.

Per-chromosome panels: pass any one chromosome's file (e.g. ALL.chr3.phased.vcf.gz) and the files for the other GWAS chromosomes are found by substituting into the 'chrN' token.

Writes {out}.clumps (plink2 report), {out}.lead.tsv (index variants with their GWAS stats), {out}.dropped.tsv (unmatched GWAS variants) and {out}.log.

Examples:

c4 clump results.PHENO.glm.logistic.hybrid 1kg_EUR -o clumped/pheno

c4 clump results.assoc 1kg.chr6.vcf.gz -o out/chr6 --chr 6 --kgp-pops EUR,YRI \
    --clump-p1 1e-5 --clump-r2 0.2 --clump-kb 500

Usage:

c4 clump [OPTIONS] GWAS GENO

Options:

Can't be combined with --keep. None --keep path Sample ID file to subset the panel to (plink2 --keep format: IID, or FID IID) None --clump-p1 float Significance threshold for index variants 5e-08 --clump-p2 float Significance threshold for clumped variants 0.01 --clump-r2 float LD r² threshold for clumping 0.1 --clump-kb float Clumping window in kb 250 --chrom-col text GWAS chromosome column (default: auto-detect) None --pos-col text GWAS position column (default: auto-detect) None --ref-col text GWAS REF allele column (default: auto-detect) None --alt-col text GWAS ALT allele column (default: auto-detect) None --p-col text GWAS p-value column (default: auto-detect) None --threads integer plink2 --threads None --memory integer plink2 --memory (MiB). Default: half of the SLURM/cgroup job memory limit, if one is found None --plink2 text Path to the plink2 executable plink2 --plink1 text Path to PLINK1.9, used for clumping only if the plink2 build has no --clump plink --verbose, -v boolean Also print each plink command as it runs False --help boolean Show this message and exit. docs.title: concordance
docs.text:
Calculate genotype concordance between two variant call files.

Example: c4 concordance file1.vcf file2.bed output.tsv --within c4 concordance file1.vcf file2.bed output.tsv --samples1 samples1.txt --samples2 samples2.txt

Computes pairwise concordance between samples in two files. Optionally computes within-file concordance with --within flag.

Each between-file pair gets two rows: all_exclHomRef (sites where the file-2 sample is homozygous reference left out) and all_inclHomRef (all sites). Within-file pairs get one row, labelled "all".

Usage:

c4 concordance [OPTIONS] FILE1 FILE2 OUTPUT

Options:

Name Type Description Default --within, -w boolean Also compute within-file concordance False --samples1, -s1 path File with sample IDs to use from file1 (one per line) None --samples2, -s2 path File with sample IDs to use from file2 (one per line) None --between-pairs, -b path File containing sample ID pairs to compare between files (tab-separated: file1_ID file2_ID per line). None --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: dosages
docs.text:
Extract dosages for a few variants from a cohort's VCFs.

Each column counts copies of the ALT allele as you wrote it; if the VCF has the alleles the other way round, the dosage is flipped. Samples are linked to patient_id through the cohort's id_map.

Examples:

c4 dosages --dataset COHORT --variants 6:32659999:A:G -o hla_snp.tsv

c4 dosages --dataset COHORT --variant-list snps.txt --variant-build b37 -o snps.tsv

Usage:

c4 dosages [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --dataset, -d text Cohort name, as listed in the data catalog (c4/catalog.yaml) _required --output, -o path Output TSV: one row per sample, one column per variant. How each variant matched goes to NAME.variants.tsv next to it. _required --variants, -v text Variant(s) as chr:pos:ref:alt, 'chr:pos:ref>alt' (quote it) or chr:pos. Repeat the flag for several. None --variant-list path File with one variant per line None --variant-build text Genome build of the variants (e.g. b37). Default: the VCFs' build. None --dna text Which genetic data set of the cohort to read (a dna: entry in the catalog) imputed --dosage / --no-dosage boolean Use the DS dosage field (default) vs GT-derived dosage True --chain-file path Liftover chain to use instead of the catalog's None --keep-dropped boolean Keep samples of patients marked drop=1 in the cohort's id_map False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: finemap
docs.text:
Fine-mapping: LD reference panels built from the data catalog.

Usage:

c4 finemap [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

Subcommands

  • avail: List the genetic data sets that can be used as a panel (pass the name as
  • loci: Define the loci to fine-map from one or more GWAS.
  • run: Fine-map loci with SuSiE-RSS, using GWAS z-scores and LD from a panel
  • setup: Build an LD reference panel from a cohort's genetic data in the catalog.
  • visualize: Plot fine-mapped loci: -log10(p), PIP and genes, one figure per locus.

docs.title: avail
docs.text:
List the genetic data sets that can be used as a panel (pass the name as --dna to c4 finemap setup), and the panels already set up in --dir.

Usage:

c4 finemap avail [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --dir path Where panels are written (default: $TMPDIR) None --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: loci
docs.text:
Define the loci to fine-map from one or more GWAS.

Every variant with p < --p gets a window of ±--window; overlapping windows are merged, pooling all traits, so a locus doesn't depend on which trait found it. All variants in a locus are fine-mapped later, whatever their p-value. With --build, windows touching the extended MHC become one MHC locus.

Locus IDs are coordinates (6:31500000-32500000), so they stay the same between runs. Each row also has the lead variant across traits, the number of significant variants, each trait's minimum p, and is_mhc / exceeds_max_width flags. Edit the file, or write your own, to fine-map other regions.

Examples:

c4 finemap loci results.PHENO.glm.logistic.hybrid --build b38 -o loci.tsv

c4 finemap loci te1.tsv te2.tsv --trait TE1 --trait TE2 --build b38 --p 1e-6 --window 1mb -o loci.tsv

Usage:

c4 finemap loci [OPTIONS] GWAS...

Options:

Name Type Description Default --out, -o path Output TSV of loci _required --build text Genome build of the GWAS positions (b37 or b38), used to merge the MHC into one locus None --p float A locus is built around every variant with p below this 5e-08 --window text Window on each side of a significant variant (e.g. 500kb, 1mb, 250000) 500kb --max-width text Flag loci wider than this (they are not split) 3mb --skip-mhc boolean Leave the MHC locus out of the output False --trait text Trait name for each GWAS file, in order (repeat the option). Default: from the file name None --trait-col text Column holding the trait, for files with several traits None --chrom-col text GWAS chromosome column (default: auto-detect) None --pos-col text GWAS position column (default: auto-detect) None --p-col text GWAS p-value column (default: auto-detect) None --verbose, -v boolean More progress output False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: run
docs.text:
Fine-map loci with SuSiE-RSS, using GWAS z-scores and LD from a panel built with c4 finemap setup.

For each locus, every GWAS variant in it (whatever its p-value) is matched to the panel on position and alleles, z is oriented to the panel ALT allele, LD is computed from the panel dosages, and susie_rss is run in R. estimate_s_rss and kriging_rss check that the z-scores fit the LD (allele flips, panel mismatch).

Writes {out}.cs.tsv (one row per credible set, with purity, the lead variant by PIP and by p, and the minimum p), {out}.cs_members.tsv (full GWAS row for every member), {out}.pip.tsv (every variant), {out}.summary.tsv (one row per locus: status, counts, drop reasons, s), {out}.dropped.tsv and {out}.run.json.

If the GWAS was run on the panel's own genotypes (e.g. a GWAS of the demo cohort, with a panel built from demo.imputed), say so with --in-sample: SuSiE then estimates the residual variance, --drop-ambiguous is refused, and loci whose N differs from the panel's sample count, or with kriging flags, get a note in summary.tsv.

Needs R with susieR (on C4: module load r).

Examples:

c4 finemap run results.PHENO.glm.logistic.hybrid --loci loci.tsv --panel kgp_eur --build b38 -o fm/pheno

c4 finemap run demo_gwas.glm.linear --loci loci.tsv --panel demo --build b38 \
    --in-sample --locus 6:31500000-32500000 -o fm/one_locus

Usage:

c4 finemap run [OPTIONS] GWAS

Options:

Name Type Description Default --loci path Loci to fine-map: the output of c4 finemap loci, or any TSV with chrom, start, end _required --panel text LD panel name, as given to c4 finemap setup --panel-name _required --build text Genome build of the GWAS (b37 or b38); must match the panel _required --out, -o path Output prefix _required --dir path Where the panel is (default: $TMPDIR) None --locus text Only this locus_id (repeat the option for several) None --n float GWAS sample size. Default: the median OBS_CT/N of each locus's variants None --L integer SuSiE L: maximum number of causal signals per locus 10 --coverage float Credible set coverage 0.95 --min-abs-corr float Purity: credible sets whose minimum r --in-sample boolean The GWAS was run on the panel's own genotypes (not allowed for a reference panel such as kgp) False --estimate-residual-variance / --fixed-residual-variance boolean Let SuSiE estimate the residual variance. Default: yes with --in-sample, no otherwise None --drop-ambiguous boolean Leave out strand-ambiguous SNPs (A/T, C/G); not allowed with in-sample LD. They are always flagged False --max-variants integer Skip loci with more variants than this 20000 --chrom-col text GWAS chromosome column (default: auto-detect) None --pos-col text GWAS position column (default: auto-detect) None --ref-col text GWAS REF allele column (default: auto-detect) None --alt-col text GWAS ALT allele column (default: auto-detect) None --p-col text GWAS p-value column (default: auto-detect) None --z-col text z-score column (default: Z_STAT, Z or T_STAT, else BETA/SE or log(OR)/SE) None --beta-col text Effect size column, used with --se-col None --se-col text Standard error column None --n-col text Per-variant sample size column (default: OBS_CT, N, ...) None --ea-col text Effect allele column (default: A1, EFFECT_ALLELE or ALLELE1, else ALT) None --rscript text Path to Rscript (with susieR installed) Rscript --verbose, -v boolean Also print each Rscript command, and tracebacks for failed loci False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: setup
docs.text:
Build an LD reference panel from a cohort's genetic data in the catalog.

Writes one plink2 fileset per chromosome to //chr.pgen (variant IDs CHROM:POS:REF:ALT, dosages kept), plus samples.keep and settings.json. defaults to $TMPDIR, so the panel lasts as long as the session or job.

Samples: the id_map's IDs for that data set, minus patients marked drop=1, narrowed by --pops and --keep if given. For 1000 Genomes (kgp.b38, kgp.b37) that is the 2,504 unrelated phase 3 samples.

Running again with the same --panel-name adds chromosomes. If the panel was built with different settings, or a chromosome is already there, you are asked before it is overwritten (--force skips the question).

Examples:

c4 finemap avail

c4 finemap setup --dna demo.imputed --panel-name demo --chr 6 --maf 0.001

c4 finemap setup --dna kgp.b38 --panel-name kgp_eur --pops EUR --chr 6

c4 finemap setup --dna demo.imputed --panel-name demo_eur --keep eur.txt --dir /scratch/me

Usage:

c4 finemap setup [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --dna text Genetic data set, as . (e.g. demo.imputed). See c4 finemap avail. _required --panel-name text Name of the panel; files go to // _required --dir path Where to write the panel (default: $TMPDIR) None --chr text Chromosome(s) to build, e.g. 6 or 6,7 (default: 1-22) None --keep path Only these samples (plink --keep format: IID, or FID IID), within the id_map samples not marked drop=1 None --pops text Comma-separated populations and/or super-populations to keep (e.g. EUR or GBR,CEU), from the pheno pop/super_pop columns of a reference panel such as kgp None --maf float plink2 --maf: minimum minor allele frequency None --mac integer plink2 --mac: minimum minor allele count None --geno float plink2 --geno: maximum per-variant missingness None --hwe float plink2 --hwe: HWE p-value threshold None --plink-args text Any other plink2 arguments, quoted, e.g. "--snps-only just-acgt" None --dosage / --hardcalls boolean Import FORMAT/DS dosages (default: if the VCF has DS) None --force, -f boolean Overwrite an existing panel or chromosome without asking False --threads integer plink2 --threads None --memory integer plink2 --memory (MiB). Default: half of the SLURM/cgroup job memory limit, if one is found None --plink2 text Path to the plink2 executable plink2 --verbose, -v boolean Also print each plink2 command as it runs False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: visualize
docs.text:
Plot fine-mapped loci: -log10(p), PIP and genes, one figure per locus.

Points are coloured by r² with the nearest credible-set lead (LocusZoom colours; --color-by top uses the top-PIP variant instead). Credible-set members get one marker shape per set, leads are purple diamonds, and kriging-flagged variants have a black ring. The title line gives the number of variants, N, credible sets, s and the LD source.

Uses only the run's outputs, so the LD panel doesn't need to exist any more. LD colours need a run made with this version of c4 (older runs plot in grey).

Examples:

c4 finemap visualize fm/pheno -o plots/

c4 finemap visualize fm/pheno -o plots/ --locus 6:31500000-32500000 --format pdf

Usage:

c4 finemap visualize [OPTIONS] PREFIX

Options:

Name Type Description Default --out, -o path Directory for the plots (one file per locus) _required --locus text Only this locus_id (repeat the option for several) None --all boolean Also plot loci without a credible set False --full-locus boolean Show the whole locus window (default: just the span of its variants, plus a margin) False --format text png, pdf or svg png --color-by text cs: r² with the nearest credible-set lead; top: r² with the top-PIP variant cs --genes / --no-genes boolean Draw the gene track True --gtf path GTF for the gene track (default: the catalog's GTF for the run's build) None --all-biotypes boolean Show every gene, not only protein-coding ones False --verbose, -v boolean More progress output False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: genotype-correlation
docs.text:
Compute per-sample Pearson r and r² between dosage vectors across two VCFs.

Matches samples by ID (or by mapping file) and computes correlation across all overlapping variants (matched on CHROM, POS, REF, ALT).

Examples:

c4 genotype-correlation vcf1.vcf.gz vcf2.vcf.gz output.tsv

c4 genotype-correlation vcf1.vcf.gz vcf2.vcf.gz output.tsv --dosage

c4 genotype-correlation vcf1.vcf.gz vcf2.vcf.gz output.tsv \
    --samples samples.txt --positions positions.txt --verbose

Usage:

c4 genotype-correlation [OPTIONS] VCF1 VCF2 OUTPUT

Options:

Name Type Description Default --dosage boolean Use DS field if present in VCF; falls back to GT if absent. False --samples, -s path Optional sample file. Single column: sample IDs to use from both VCFs. Two columns (tab-separated): VCF1 ID -> VCF2 ID mapping. None --positions, -p path Optional positions file (two columns: CHROM POS, no header) to subset variants. None --verbose, -v boolean Output Pearson sufficient statistics per sample pair (N, SUM_X, SUM_Y, SUM_X2, SUM_Y2, SUM_XY) to allow genome-wide aggregation across chromosomes. False --keep-tmp boolean Do not delete temporary files after completion (useful for debugging). False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: hla_concordance
docs.text:
Compare HLA typing between two files.

Files can have one genotype column per gene (A*01:01/02:01) or two allele columns (A_1, A_2). Prints a per-gene summary; per-sample scores go to --output, or stdout.

Example: c4 hla_concordance wes.csv imputed.csv \ --file1_id sample_id --file2_id sample_id \ --output concordance.tsv

Usage:

c4 hla_concordance [OPTIONS] FILE1 FILE2

Options:

Name Type Description Default --output, -o path Output file for per-sample results (.csv, .tsv or .txt). Default: print to stdout. None --genes, -g text Genes to compare, separated by commas (no spaces). Default: every canonical HLA gene in both files. None --file1_id text ID column name in file 1 _required --file2_id text ID column name in file 2 _required --digits, -d integer Compare at this resolution, e.g. 4 for 2-field None --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: liftover
docs.text:
Lift variant positions in a file to another genome build.

Uses pyliftover; no R needed. A .bed file's first three columns are used (0-based, as BED is). For other files give --chrom-col and --start-col; positions are taken as 1-based unless --zero-based. Output is a 3-column BED file in the input's order. Rows that can't be lifted (not in the new build, mapping to several places, or a region that splits) are written to OUTPUT.unmapped with the reason.

Examples: c4 liftover hg19ToHg38.over.chain variants.bed variants_hg38.bed c4 liftover hg19ToHg38.over.chain variants.txt variants_hg38.bed --chrom-col 0 --start-col 1

Usage:

c4 liftover [OPTIONS] CHAIN_FILE INPUT_FILE OUTPUT_BED

Options:

Name Type Description Default --chrom-col integer 0-indexed chromosome column (required unless the input is .bed) None --start-col integer 0-indexed position column (required unless the input is .bed) None --end-col integer 0-indexed end column, for regions. Default: each row is the single base at --start-col. None --zero-based boolean Table positions are 0-based (BED-style). Default: 1-based, as in VCFs. .bed input is always 0-based. False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: merge-hla
docs.text:
Merge separate allele columns back into HLA genotype columns.

Example: c4 merge-hla input.csv output.csv --genes A B C DRB1 --sep ","

Converts columns like "DRB1_1" and "DRB1_2" back into "DRB1" with "01:01/02:02"

Usage:

c4 merge-hla [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE [OUTPUT_FILE]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --genes, -g text Gene to include. Must separate by commas (no spaces). None --digits, -d integer Resolution in digits (e.g., 4 for 2-field) None --columns, -c text Non-gene columns to include. Will ONLY include these + gene columns in output. Must be separated by commas (no spaces). None --format, -f text The output text format. Options are: standard (A01:02/03:04), standard2 (A01:02/A*03:04), standard_no_gene (01:02/03:04). standard --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: prs
docs.text:
Test a weighted polygenic risk score (PRS) for survival association.

The weights file is a headerless 3-column TSV: variant_id (chr:bp:ref:alt or chr:bp:ref>alt), effect_allele, and effect (additive beta). The PRS is the weighted sum of effect-allele dosages, standardised to report HR per SD.

Examples:

c4 prs --dataset COHORT --weights prs.tsv --survival OS

c4 prs --dataset COHORT --weights prs.tsv --survival OS \
    --weight-build b37 --gt-build b38 --chain-file hg19ToHg38.chain \
    --quantiles 5 --output-dir prs_OS/

Usage:

c4 prs [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --dataset, -d text Cohort name; it needs a survival: block in the data catalog (c4/catalog.yaml) _required --weights, -w path Headerless 3-column TSV: variant_id, effect_allele, effect _required --weight-build text Genome build of the weight variants (b37 or b38) b38 --gt-build text Genome build of the genotype VCF (b37 or b38). Defaults to the dataset's build. None --chain-file path Liftover chain file (required when weight-build != gt-build) None --survival text Survival endpoint (e.g. OS, PFS) _required --keep-ambiguous / --drop-ambiguous boolean Keep palindromic (A/T, C/G) SNPs (default: drop them) False --quantiles integer If >1, also report HR of top vs bottom PRS quantile (e.g. 5) 0 --output-dir, -o path Output directory (created if needed). Writes individual PRS, a log, a PRS histogram, per-variant table, and (with --quantiles) a KM plot. _required --dosage / --no-dosage boolean Use DS dosage field (default) vs GT-derived dosage True --tmpdir path Directory for intermediate files (default: $TMPDIR) None --verbose / --no-verbose boolean Show per-variant matching detail False --save-dosages boolean Also write the weight variants' dosages to prs_dosages.tsv in the output directory (ALT-coded as in the weights file), plus prs_dosages.variants.tsv. False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.text:
Split HLA genotype columns into separate allele columns.

Example: c4 split-hla input.csv output.csv --genes A B C DRB1 --sep ","

Usage:

c4 split-hla [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE [OUTPUT_FILE]

None --digits, -d integer Resolution in digits (e.g., 4 for 2-field) None --columns, -c text Non-gene columns to include. Will ONLY include these + gene columns in output. Must be separated by commas (no spaces). None --format, -f text The output text format. Options are: standard (A01:02/03:04), standard2 (A01:02/A*03:04), standard_no_gene (01:02/03:04). standard --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: survival
docs.text:
Run Cox PH survival analysis for one or more variants.

IMPORTANT: quote any 'ref>alt' variant on the command line — an unquoted '>' is redirection to your shell, and it will silently send this command's output to a file named after the ALT allele instead of running the analysis (e.g. --variants 2:8599331:T>C with no quotes creates/overwrites a file called "C"). Either quote it (--variants '2:8599331:T>C') or use the colon-delimited form, which needs no quoting (--variants 2:8599331:T:C).

Examples:

c4 survival --dataset COHORT --variants '4:1455432:A>T' --survival OS

c4 survival --dataset COHORT --variant-list vars.txt --survival OS --output results.tsv

c4 survival --dataset COHORT --variants '4:1455432:A>T' --survival OS --km-plot km.png

c4 survival --dataset COHORT --variants '4:1455432:A>T' --survival OS --km-plot km.png --km-plot-carrier

Usage:

c4 survival [OPTIONS]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --dataset, -d text Cohort name; it needs a survival: block in the data catalog (c4/catalog.yaml) _required --variants, -v text Variant(s) in 'chr:pos:ref>alt' format. ALWAYS quote the value — unquoted '>' is redirection to your shell and will silently dump output to a file named after the ALT allele instead of running the command. Repeat the flag for multiple: --variants '4:1234:A>G' --variants '6:5678:C>T'. Alternatively use the colon-delimited form (chr:pos:ref:alt), which needs no quoting, e.g. --variants 4:1234:A:G None --variant-list path File with one variant per line (implies TSV output) None --variant-build text Genome build of the input variants (e.g. b37, b38) b38 --survival text Survival endpoint (e.g. OS, PFS) _required --output, -o path Output TSV path (required when using --variant-list) None --dosage / --no-dosage boolean Use DS dosage field (default) vs GT-derived dosage True --tmpdir path Directory for intermediate files (default: $TMPDIR) None --verbose / --no-verbose boolean Show full table (VCF ID, N, events); default shows variant, HR, p, MAF, notes only False --km-plot path Write a Kaplan-Meier plot (PNG) for this variant. Only valid when exactly one variant is given. None --km-plot-carrier boolean With --km-plot, plot just two curves — carrier (>=1 copy) vs non-carrier — instead of one curve per genotype. Useful for rare alleles where the homozygous-alt group is empty or tiny. False --save-dosages path Also write the variants' dosages to this TSV (one row per sample, one column per variant), plus NAME.variants.tsv with how each variant matched. None --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: vcf-overlap
docs.text:
Find overlapping variants between two VCF files.

Both VCF files must be indexed (.csi or .tbi). Files are automatically ordered by size (smaller loaded into memory, larger streamed).

Example: c4 vcf-overlap array.vcf.gz imputed.vcf.gz overlap.tsv c4 vcf-overlap array.vcf.gz imputed.vcf.gz overlap.tsv --no-allele c4 vcf-overlap array.vcf.gz imputed.vcf.gz overlap.tsv --remove-dup

Usage:

c4 vcf-overlap [OPTIONS] VCF1 VCF2 OUTPUT

Options:

Name Type Description Default --on-allele, -a / --no-allele, -A boolean Match on REF/ALT in addition to position True --remove-dup, -d boolean Remove duplicate positions False --help boolean Show this message and exit. False

docs.title: Fine-mapping
docs.text:
c4 finemap fine-maps GWAS loci with SuSiE-RSS. For each locus it reports credible sets (small groups of variants that very likely contain a causal variant) and each variant's posterior inclusion probability (PIP).

It takes three steps:

Step Command What it does 1 c4 finemap setup Builds an LD reference panel from a cohort's genotypes, or from 1000 Genomes 2 c4 finemap loci Turns GWAS hits into regions to fine-map 3 c4 finemap run Matches each region's GWAS variants to the panel and runs SuSiE 4 c4 finemap visualize Plots each locus: p-values, PIPs and genes

You need plink2 for step 1, and R with susieR for step 3. On C4:

module load plink2 r

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# 1. A panel from the cohort the GWAS was run on (chr6 only)
c4 finemap setup --dna demo.imputed --panel-name demo --chr 6 --maf 0.001

# 2. ±500 kb around every p < 5e-8 variant
c4 finemap loci results.PHENO.glm.linear --build b38 -o loci.tsv

# 3. SuSiE on each locus
c4 finemap run results.PHENO.glm.linear --loci loci.tsv --panel demo --build b38 \
    --in-sample -o fm/pheno

Then look at fm/pheno.cs.tsv for the credible sets, and at fm/pheno.summary.tsv to check that every locus ran cleanly. To plot every locus that has a credible set:

c4 finemap visualize fm/pheno -o plots/

docs.title: 1. Build an LD panel
docs.text:
SuSiE needs the correlation (LD) between the variants in each locus. It gets it from a panel: a set of genotypes that setup converts to plink2 files.

c4 finemap avail

avail lists every genetic data set in the data catalog, named <cohort>.<entry>, plus any panels you have already built:

Genetic data in the catalog (use the first column as --dna):

          dna      kind format build chroms status source
 demo.imputed    cohort    vcf   b38   1-22  22/22 ✓
  demo.exome     cohort      -     -      -  not set
      kgp.b38 reference    vcf   b38   1-22  22/22 ✓ https://ftp.1000genomes.ebi.ac.uk/...
      kgp.b37 reference    vcf   b37   1-22  22/22 ✓ https://ftp.1000genomes.ebi.ac.uk/...

Then build a panel from one of them:

# The GWAS cohort's own genotypes (best, if the GWAS was run on them)
c4 finemap setup --dna demo.imputed --panel-name demo --chr 6

# 1000 Genomes, European samples only
c4 finemap setup --dna kgp.b38 --panel-name kgp_eur --pops EUR --chr 6

Use the GWAS cohort itself when you can

SuSiE-RSS is sensitive to differences between the panel's LD and the LD in the GWAS samples. If you have the genotypes the GWAS was run on, a panel built from them (in-sample LD) is much more reliable than 1000 Genomes.

Where it goes. Panels are written to $TMPDIR/<panel-name>/, one set of plink2 files per chromosome (chr6.pgen/.pvar/.psam), plus samples.keep and settings.json. On Slurm, $TMPDIR is deleted when the job ends, so build the panel in the same job that uses it (see Running it as a Slurm job). Use --dir to put it somewhere else.

Samples. The panel uses the cohort's samples for that data set from its ID map, minus patients marked drop=1. You can narrow that:

  • --keep file.txt keeps only those samples (plink format: IID, or FID IID).
  • --pops EUR (or --pops GBR,CEU) keeps populations or super-populations, for reference panels such as 1000 Genomes.

For 1000 Genomes, kgp.b38 (30x high coverage) and kgp.b37 (phase 3) both give the same 2,504 unrelated samples. The b38 VCFs' 698 extra samples, mostly relatives, are marked drop=1.

Variants. Variant IDs are CHROM:POS:REF:ALT. Imputed dosages (DS) are kept when the VCF has them, and LD is then computed from dosages rather than hard calls. Optional filters: --maf, --mac, --geno, --hwe, and --plink-args "..." for anything else plink2 takes. Records with more than two alleles are dropped (imputed VCFs are already split), as are repeated records of the same variant.

Running again. Running setup again with the same --panel-name adds chromosomes. If the panel was built with different settings, or a chromosome you asked for is already there, you're asked before anything is overwritten. --force skips the question, and batch jobs need it.

docs.title: 2. Define the loci
docs.text:
c4 finemap loci results.PHENO.glm.linear --build b38 -o loci.tsv

Every variant with p < --p (default 5e-8) gets a window of --window (default 500 kb) on each side. Overlapping windows are merged into one locus.

  • --p only decides where the loci are. Every variant inside a locus is fine-mapped, whatever its p-value. SuSiE needs the non-significant variants to model the LD.
  • Windows are merged by distance, not by LD. Two nearby signals end up in one locus, and SuSiE separates them. This is different from clumping, which would split them.
  • Locus IDs are coordinates, such as 6:31500000-32500000, so they stay the same between runs and when you add traits.
  • The MHC is one locus. With --build, any window that touches the extended MHC (b37 chr6:28,477,797-33,448,354; b38 chr6:28,510,120-33,480,577) is merged into a single MHC locus, marked is_mhc. SuSiE results there are hard to interpret because of the MHC's extreme LD; --skip-mhc leaves it out.
  • Wide loci are flagged, not split. Loci wider than --max-width (3 Mb) are marked exceeds_max_width.

Several traits. Give several GWAS files and the loci are pooled across them. A locus doesn't depend on which trait found it, which is what colocalization needs later.

c4 finemap loci trait1.tsv trait2.tsv --trait T1 --trait T2 --build b38 -o loci.tsv

Trait names come from the plink2 phenotype in the file name, or from --trait. For a single file holding several traits, use --trait-col.

loci.tsv has one row per locus:

Column Meaning locus_id, chrom, start, end, width The region lead_id, lead_p, lead_trait Most significant variant in the region, across traits n_sig Number of distinct variants with p < --p traits, trait_min_p Each trait with a hit, and its minimum p is_mhc, exceeds_max_width Flags

You can edit this file, or write your own with chrom, start and end columns, to fine-map other regions.

docs.title: 3. Run SuSiE
docs.text:
c4 finemap run results.PHENO.glm.linear --loci loci.tsv --panel demo --build b38 \
    --in-sample -o fm/pheno

For each locus, run:

  1. Takes every GWAS variant in the region.
  2. Matches it to a panel variant on position and alleles. An exact REF/ALT match is preferred; a swapped match is accepted when it's the only one. Preferring exact matches matters for indels: an insertion and a deletion at the same position, such as C/CA and CA/C, have the same two alleles.
  3. Orients z to the panel's ALT allele, so z and LD use the same allele.
  4. Computes LD from the panel's dosages.
  5. Runs susie_rss in R, along with two checks that the z-scores fit the LD (see Checking the results).

If one locus fails or is skipped, the others still run; summary.tsv says what happened to each one.

Use unfiltered summary statistics. SuSiE needs every variant in a locus, including the null ones, to model the LD. Sumstats cut down to significant or suggestive hits make PIPs and credible sets overconfident. run warns when the GWAS's largest p-value is below 0.1, and notes any locus whose variants all have p < 1e-3.

--build must match the panel. The run stops if the GWAS build and the panel's build (from its settings.json) differ.

Where z, N and the effect allele come from. z is read from Z_STAT, Z or T_STAT, else computed as BETA/SE, else log(OR)/SE. The effect allele is A1, EFFECT_ALLELE or ALLELE1, else ALT. The sample size is the median OBS_CT or N of the locus's variants, unless you give --n. The --*-col options override any of these. plink2 .glm files work as they are.

--in-sample. Use it when the GWAS was run on the panel's own genotypes. It's refused for reference panels such as 1000 Genomes. With it:

  • SuSiE estimates the residual variance, as susieR recommends for in-sample LD. --fixed-residual-variance turns that off.
  • --drop-ambiguous is refused, because the strand can't differ between the GWAS and the panel.
  • A locus whose GWAS N differs from the panel's sample count by more than 5%, or that has kriging flags, gets a note in summary.tsv. With true in-sample LD neither should happen.

Other options. --locus ID runs only that locus, and can be repeated. --L is the maximum number of signals per locus (default 10). --coverage (default 0.95) and --min-abs-corr (default 0.5, the purity cut-off) control credible sets. --max-variants (default 20,000) skips very large loci.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
All files start with the -o prefix.

File One row per .cs.tsv Credible set: size, coverage, purity, log10 Bayes factor, lead variant by PIP, lead variant and minimum p by GWAS p .cs_members.tsv Credible set member, with its full GWAS row, PIP and alpha .pip.tsv Fine-mapped variant: z, p, PIP, credible set, r² with the top variant and with the nearest credible-set lead, kriging diagnostics, strand-ambiguity flag .summary.tsv Locus: status, variant counts, drop reasons, N used, LD source, s, number of credible sets, notes .dropped.tsv GWAS variant in a locus that wasn't fine-mapped, with DROP_REASON .run.json The run: inputs, panel settings, parameters, susieR version

Credible set IDs are <locus_id>:L<k>, for example 6:31500000-32500000:L1.

Reading cs.tsv.

  • Purity (min_abs_corr, mean_abs_corr) is the LD between the set's members. Sets below --min-abs-corr are already removed. A pure set means its variants are hard to tell apart, not that the signal is weak.
  • Two leads. lead_pip_variant is SuSiE's best guess at the causal variant. lead_p_variant and min_p are the most significant GWAS variant in the set. They often differ, and both are useful.
  • Full GWAS rows. cs_members.tsv has the full GWAS row for every member, so you don't have to look members up again.

docs.title: Checking the results
docs.text:
Check summary.tsv before trusting a locus's credible sets.

Column What to look for status ok, or why the locus was skipped or failed n_gwas, n_matched, n_variants GWAS variants in the region, matched to the panel, and fine-mapped. A large gap means much of the locus is missing from the panel dropped Counts by reason (see below) s From estimate_s_rss: how inconsistent the z-scores and LD are. Near 0 is good; above about 0.1–0.2, read the locus with caution n_kriging_flagged Variants whose z doesn't fit the LD (see below) notes Warnings: every variant has p < 1e-3 (the GWAS looks filtered by p-value); with --in-sample, an N mismatch or kriging flags

Kriging flags. kriging_rss predicts each variant's z-score from its neighbours' z-scores and the panel LD. A variant is flagged (kriging_flag in pip.tsv) when its observed z fits much better with its alleles flipped (logLR > 2) and it has a real signal (|z| > 2). Common causes:

  • One or two flagged variants with a strong z: an allele flip in the sumstats, a strand-ambiguous SNP (check ambiguous_strand), or a badly imputed variant.
  • Many flagged variants across the locus: the panel doesn't match the GWAS samples, for example a different ancestry. Use in-sample LD if you can.

Why variants are dropped (DROP_REASON in dropped.tsv):

Reason Meaning not_in_panel No panel variant at that position allele_mismatch A panel variant at that position, but with different alleles ambiguous Matches more than one panel variant, and the alleles can't decide which. With REF/ALT given this is rare; with only A1 it happens at multi-allelic sites duplicate_in_gwas Another GWAS row matched the same panel variant; the more significant one is kept missing_p, missing_pos, missing_z Missing or unreadable values effect_allele_mismatch The effect allele is neither panel allele monomorphic_in_panel No variation among the panel's samples, so it has no LD strand_ambiguous A/T or C/G SNP, dropped because of --drop-ambiguous

docs.title: Plotting a locus
docs.text:
c4 finemap visualize fm/pheno -o plots/                       # every locus with a credible set
c4 finemap visualize fm/pheno -o plots/ --locus 6:31500000-32500000 --format pdf

Each plot has three panels sharing the x-axis:

  • −log₁₀(p), a local Manhattan plot, with the genome-wide significance line.
  • PIP, SuSiE's posterior inclusion probability.
  • Genes, protein-coding genes from the catalog's Ensembl GTF for the run's build (--all-biotypes for every gene, --gtf for another file, --no-genes to leave the track out).

In both data panels:

  • Colour is r² with the nearest credible-set lead, in the usual LocusZoom bins. Each signal gets its own red cloud around its own lead. --color-by top uses r² with the single top-PIP variant instead.
  • Shape: credible-set members get one marker per set (triangle for L1, square for L2, …). Each set's lead (top PIP) is a purple diamond, labelled with its ID.
  • Black ring: the variant is kriging-flagged (see Checking the results).

The title gives the number of variants, N, the number of credible sets, s, any kriging flags, and whether the LD was in-sample. The MHC is shaded on chr6.

The x-axis spans the locus's fine-mapped variants plus a small margin; --full-locus shows the whole locus window instead.

Plots are drawn from the run's output files, so the LD panel doesn't need to exist any more: you can make them after the Slurm job has finished, or on another machine. --all also plots loci without a credible set.

docs.title: Running it as a Slurm job
docs.text:
Because the panel lives in $TMPDIR, build it and use it in the same job:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=finemap
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00

module load plink2 r

c4 finemap setup --dna demo.imputed --panel-name demo --force
c4 finemap loci results.PHENO.glm.linear --build b38 -o loci.tsv
c4 finemap run results.PHENO.glm.linear --loci loci.tsv --panel demo --build b38 \
    --in-sample -o fm/pheno
c4 finemap visualize fm/pheno -o plots/

To save time, build only the chromosomes your loci are on, e.g. --chr 6,19.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
The same steps are available as functions; see the API reference.

from c4.finemap import setup_panel, find_loci, run_finemap

setup_panel("demo.imputed", "demo", chrom="6")
loci, _ = find_loci(["results.PHENO.glm.linear"], "loci.tsv", build="b38")
result = run_finemap("results.PHENO.glm.linear", "loci.tsv", "demo", "b38", "fm/pheno",
                     in_sample=True)
result["cs"]          # the credible sets, as a DataFrame

docs.title: HLA calls
docs.text: c4 reads HLA typing from HLA-HD, HIBAG and the lab's standardized files. Every loader gives you the same thing: one column per gene, holding HLAgenotype objects. Each object knows its gene, its two alleles and its resolution. It can print itself in any format, count copies of an allele, and compare itself to another call.

docs.title: Load HLA calls
docs.text:
HLA tables are in the catalog under hla, one block per caller. Load them like any other table:

from c4.cohort import cohort

demo = cohort("demo")
hla = demo.load("hla.hlahd", verbose=False)
hla[["patient_id", "seqID", "A", "B", "DRB1"]]

  patient_id    seqID                A                B                   DRB1
0       P001  EX-0001  A*02:01/A*24:02  B*07:02/B*44:02  DRB1*04:01/DRB1*15:01
1       P002  EX-0002  A*01:01/A*03:01  B*08:01/B*35:01  DRB1*01:01/DRB1*03:01
2       P004  EX-0003  A*02:01/A*02:01  B*44:03/B*51:01  DRB1*07:01/DRB1*13:01
3       P003  EX-0004  A*11:01/A*24:02  B*40:01/B*46:01  DRB1*09:01/DRB1*12:02
4       P005  EX-0005  A*03:01/A*68:01  B*07:02/B*15:01  DRB1*11:01/DRB1*15:01

The gene columns look like text, but each cell is an HLAgenotype. The two alleles are always stored in sorted order, so DRB1*15:01/04:01 in the file becomes DRB1*04:01/DRB1*15:01.

How a file is read depends on its catalog entry's loader:

Loader Used for Reads HLA every entry under hla: unless it says otherwise gene columns A (A*02:01/24:02) or allele pairs A_1, A_2 HLA-HD HLA-HD output same as HLA HIBAG raw HIBAG output allele1_A and allele2_A, plus prob_A

Only genes in config.hla_genes (A, B, C, DRB1, DQA1, DQB1, DPB1) are turned into genotypes. Any other column is left as it is in the file.

docs.title: HIBAG probabilities
docs.text:
HIBAG output has one file per reference panel. Each genotype loaded from it carries HIBAG's posterior probability as .prob. The prob_A column is kept too:

hibag = demo.load("hla.hibag", panel="african", verbose=False)
hibag.loc[0, "A"].prob

0.97

docs.title: Work with a genotype
docs.text:
gt = hla.loc[0, "A"]
gt

HLAgenotype('A*02:01/A*24:02')

str(gt) gives A*02:01/A*24:02. For another layout, use genotype():

Call Result gt.genotype(format="standard2") 'A*02:01/A*24:02' gt.genotype(format="standard") 'A*02:01/24:02' gt.genotype(format="standard_no_gene") '02:01/24:02' gt.genotype(format="tuple") (('02', '01'), ('24', '02')) gt.genotype() the two alleles, as HLAallele objects

Pass digits to get a lower resolution. Two digits make one field, so 4 is 2-field:

g = HLAgenotype("A*11:01:01/24:02:01")
g.genotype(format="standard2", digits=4)

'A*11:01/A*24:02'

Other useful attributes:

Attribute Meaning gt.a1, gt.a2 the two alleles (HLAallele), missing one last gt.gene "A" gt.fields resolution of the lower-resolution allele, in fields gt.missing_alleles 0, 1 or 2

A missing allele is written ., so A*02:01/. has one missing allele. A blank cell becomes ./..

docs.title: Allele dosages
docs.text:
copies_of() counts how many of the two alleles match, which gives an allele dosage for association tests:

hla["A"].map(lambda gt: gt.copies_of("A*02:01"))

0    1
1    0
2    2
3    0
4    0
Name: A, dtype: int64

Save it as a column with hla["A*02:01"] = ....

The match is made at the resolution of the allele you ask about, so copies_of("A*02:01") also counts A*02:01:01, and copies_of("A*02") counts every A*02 allele (the 1-field allele group).

Rows with no HLA call

After a merge, patients with no row in the HLA table have NaN in the gene columns, not a genotype. Check before calling a method:

from c4.hla import HLAgenotype

df = demo.load("pheno", "hla.hlahd", verbose=False)
df["A*02:01"] = df["A"].map(
    lambda gt: gt.copies_of("A*02:01") if isinstance(gt, HLAgenotype) else float("nan")
)

docs.title: Compare two callers
docs.text:
concordance() scores how well two calls for the same gene agree:

Score Meaning 2 both alleles match 1 one allele matches 0 neither matches NaN either call is missing an allele

The two calls are compared at the lower of their resolutions, so A*11:01:01 and A*11:01:02 match as 11:01. Pass digits=4 to compare at no more than 2-field.

To compare HLA-HD and HIBAG patient by patient, load both. They share the column A, so the second table's copy is prefixed with its name:

both = demo.load("hla.hlahd", "hla.hibag", how="inner", verbose=False)
both["A_concordance"] = [
    a.concordance(b) for a, b in zip(both["A"], both["hla.hibag.raw.A"])
]
both[["patient_id", "A", "hla.hibag.raw.A", "A_concordance"]]

  patient_id                A  hla.hibag.raw.A  A_concordance
0       P001  A*02:01/A*24:02  A*02:01/A*24:02              2
1       P002  A*01:01/A*03:01  A*01:01/A*03:01              2
2       P004  A*02:01/A*02:01  A*02:01/A*02:01              2
3       P003  A*11:01/A*24:02  A*11:01/A*24:02              2

For two files that aren't in the catalog, use c4 hla_concordance instead.

docs.title: Change table layout
docs.text:
Some tools want one column per allele (A_1, A_2) rather than one per gene. split_genotype and merge_genotype convert between the two, and both return objects:

from c4.hla import split_genotype, merge_genotype

split = split_genotype(hla, gene_list=["A", "B"])    # A -> A_1, A_2 (HLAallele)
merged = merge_genotype(split, gene_list=["A", "B"]) # A_1, A_2 -> A (HLAgenotype)

docs.title: Save to a file
docs.text:
Writing a table with to_csv saves each genotype as A*02:01/A*24:02. For another format, convert the columns first:

out = hla.copy()
for gene in ["A", "B", "DRB1"]:
    out[gene] = out[gene].map(lambda gt: gt.genotype(format="standard_no_gene", digits=4))
out.to_csv("hla_2field.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)

c4 reads a saved file back into genotypes, in any of these text formats.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: The c4 command converts and compares HLA files without writing Python. Every command reads .csv, .tsv or space-separated files. Each file can have genotype columns (A) or allele columns (A_1, A_2).

docs.title: c4 split-hla
docs.text:
Genotype columns to allele columns. With no output file, the result is printed:

c4 split-hla calls.csv --genes A,B --columns ID --digits 4

  ID     A_1     A_2     B_1     B_2
S001 A*01:01       . B*07:02 B*08:01
S002 A*02:01 A*03:01       .       .
...

Give an output file to save it instead: c4 split-hla calls.csv calls_split.tsv ....

docs.title: c4 merge-hla
docs.text:
Allele columns to genotype columns:

c4 merge-hla calls_split.csv calls.tsv --genes A,B --columns ID

Options for both commands:

Option Default Description --genes, -g all canonical genes Comma-separated genes, e.g. A,B,DRB1 --columns, -c every column Other columns to keep, comma-separated --digits, -d all fields Resolution, e.g. 4 for 2-field --format, -f standard standard (A*02:01/24:02), standard2 (A*02:01/A*24:02) or standard_no_gene (02:01/24:02)

docs.title: c4 hla_concordance
docs.text:
Compare two typing files, sample by sample:

c4 hla_concordance wes.csv imputed.tsv \
    --file1_id seqID --file2_id IID \
    --genes A,B --digits 4 --output concordance.tsv

3 IDs in both files (1 only in file 1, 1 only in file 2)
gene  compared  full  partial  none  allele_concordance
   A         3     2        1     0               0.833
   B         2     1        1     0               0.750
✓ Concordance results saved: concordance.tsv

concordance.tsv has one row per ID found in both files, with A_file1, A_file2 and A_concordance for each gene. allele_concordance is the number of matching alleles divided by the number compared.

Option Default Description --file1_id, --file2_id (required) ID column in each file --genes, -g every canonical gene in both files Comma-separated genes --digits, -d all fields Compare at no more than this resolution --output, -o print Per-sample results file

The two files can use different ID columns, but the IDs themselves must match. To link exome and array IDs, load both through the catalog instead (How IDs link).

See c4.hla for every class and function.

docs.title: From R
docs.text: The c4r package loads data from R through the same data catalog as Python's cohort(), and returns ordinary data.frames. It is a thin wrapper: the Python c4 package does the work, through reticulate.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
You need the Python install first (setup), plus the R package reticulate. Then, from the root of the c4 repository:

R CMD INSTALL c4r

or, in R, install.packages("c4r", repos = NULL, type = "source").

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
Tell c4r which Python has c4 installed, once per session:

library(c4r)
c4r_setup(python = "/path/to/venv/bin/python")   # or a virtualenv directory

To skip this step, set C4_PYTHON in ~/.Renviron:

C4_PYTHON=/path/to/venv/bin/python

To use another catalog, e.g. the demo one, pass it to setup: c4r_setup(catalog = "examples/demo/catalog.yaml").

Check the setup

From the repository root, C4_PYTHON=/path/to/venv/bin/python Rscript c4r/tests/run_demo.R runs every method on the demo cohort and ends with "All c4r checks passed."

docs.title: Load data
docs.text:
The cohort object has the same methods as in Python, called with $ instead of .. The examples use the fake demo cohort, shown with its data folder as /data/lab.

c4_cohorts()

[1] "demo"

demo <- cohort("demo")          # prints what's available, as in Python
pheno <- demo$load("pheno")
str(pheno)

Left out 1 patient(s) marked drop=1 in the id_map (keep_dropped=True to keep them).
'data.frame':   7 obs. of  8 variables:
 $ patient_id: chr  "P001" "P002" "P003" "P004" ...
 $ qc_note   : chr  NA NA "old exome_id: EX-0003" "old exome_id: EX-0004" ...
 $ ID        : chr  "P001" "P002" "P003" "P004" ...
 $ age       : int  64 58 71 66 49 73 55

df <- demo$load("pheno", "pcs", "hla.hlahd")
df[, c("patient_id", "OS_mo", "IID", "PC1", "seqID", "A")]

Note: 1 of 7 rows in 'pcs' have no patient_id (array ID not in id_map).

+ hla.hlahd.standardized          5 matched   (2 without)

1       P001  31.2 ARR-0001  0.012 EX-0001 A*02:01/A*24:02
2       P002  44.0 ARR-0002  0.010 EX-0002 A*01:01/A*03:01
